description:
Ardoe House, sometimes called Ardoe Castle, stands on the banks of the River Dee at Blairs in Royal Deeside, a few miles from Aberdeen; Balmoral lies further up the same valley. The estate is first recorded in 1244, when Alexander II granted it to Arbroath Abbey. In 1631 it was bought by the Rev. William Guild, chaplain to King Charles I; Aberdeen's Guild Street is named after him.

In 1839 the estate was bought by the Aberdeen soap merchant Alexander Ogston, known as "Soapy" Ogston. His son, also Alexander, built the present house in 1878. The architect was James Matthews, who took inspiration from Balmoral. The house stayed in the family until 1947, when it became a hotel.

A local legend says the hotel is haunted by a "White Lady", linked to a painting of Katherine Ogston, wife of a former owner. The hotel closed in late 2020 and reopened in June 2021 under new management as Ardoe House Hotel & Spa.

Ardoe House Hotel & Spa is a 4-star hotel set in gardens beside the Dee, with a Drawing Room and a Whisky Bar. It serves afternoon tea, and its restaurant has long been popular with Aberdeen locals as well as hotel guests; book ahead. Rooms are in the historic house and later additions.

faqs.question: What is the history of Ardoe House?
faqs.answer: The estate dates to 1244, when Alexander II granted it to Arbroath Abbey. In 1631 it was bought by the Rev. William Guild, chaplain to King Charles I, and in 1839 by the soap merchant Alexander Ogston. His son, also Alexander, built the present house in 1878. It was a family home until 1947, when it became a hotel, and it reopened in June 2021 as Ardoe House Hotel & Spa.

faqs.question: Who built Ardoe House?
faqs.answer: Alexander Ogston, son of the Aberdeen soap merchant known as "Soapy" Ogston, built the present house in 1878. The architect was James Matthews.

faqs.question: Is Ardoe House haunted?
faqs.answer: Local legend says the hotel is haunted by a "White Lady", linked to a painting of Katherine Ogston, wife of a former owner.

faqs.question: Can you have afternoon tea at Ardoe House without staying?
faqs.answer: Ardoe House serves afternoon tea, and its restaurant has long been popular with Aberdeen locals as well as hotel guests; book ahead.

faqs.question: Why does Ardoe House look like Balmoral?
faqs.answer: The architect James Matthews took inspiration from Balmoral when he designed the house for the Ogston family in 1878. Balmoral, rebuilt for Queen Victoria and Prince Albert, helped popularise the Scots Baronial style.

faqs.question: Who was 'Soapy' Ogston?
faqs.answer: Alexander Ogston, nicknamed "Soapy", was the Aberdeen soap merchant who bought the Ardoe estate in 1839. His son, also Alexander, built the present house in 1878.
